results.title: Solving sparse multi-objective optimization problems via dynamic adaptive grouping and reward-penalty sparse strategies - ScienceDirect
results.content: # Solving sparse multi-objective optimization problems via dynamic adaptive grouping and reward-penalty sparse strategies☆. While evolutionary algorithms have shown good performance in tackling complex problems, many algorithms tend to exhibit performance degradation when dealing with SMOPs. The primary reasons for this performance decline are the curse of dimensionality and the inability to effectively leverage the sparsity of Pareto-optimal solutions. To address this issue, this paper proposes a model method to solve sparse multi-objective optimization problems through dynamic adaptive grouping and reward-penalty sparse strategies. These problems involve a large number of decision variables, and the Pareto optimal solutions often contain many zero decision variables. However, in the past few decades, researchers have primarily focused on solving large-scale multi-objective optimization problems (LMOPs), with comparatively less attention given to SMOPs. Traditional multi-objective evolutionary algorithms (MOEAs) [6], [7], [8] tend to experience performance degradation as the dimensionality of the problem increases. Firstly, there are evolutionary algorithms based on the strategy of grouping decision variables [9], [10], [11], which solve the problems by dividing the decision variables into several subgroups and employing a divide-and-conquer strategy. To this aim, this paper proposes an algorithm for solving Sparse Multi-Objective Optimization Problems through dynamic adaptive grouping and reward-penalty sparse strategies (DPREA), with the following main contributions:. (1) Sparse initialization strategy: Due to the sparsity property of Pareto optimal solutions in SMOPs, this paper proposes a “Cover All Sparsity” initialization strategy in the initialization phase to obtain more prior information about the sparsity of optimal solutions. Fig. 1 illustrates the proposed multi-objective evolutionary algorithm framework based on decision variable scores in this paper. For SMOPs, the DPREA algorithm proposed in this paper first uses sparse initialization to generate a sparse population and obtain the scores of decision variables by integrating the population information. ### An evolutionary algorithm based on dynamic sparse grouping for sparse large scale multiobjective optimization. ### A survey of evolutionary algorithms for multi-objective optimization problems with irregular pareto fronts. ### IEEE/ CAA J. ### A survey of evolutionary algorithms for multi-objective optimization problems with irregular pareto fronts. ### A scalable indicator-based evolutionary algorithm for large-scale multiobjective optimization. ### An evolutionary algorithm for large-scale sparse multiobjective optimization problems.

results.content: What are the multi objective optimization technique? Multi-objective optimization techniques are methods used to solve optimization problems that involve multiple conflicting objectives. Multi-objective optimization techniques are methods used to solve optimization problems that involve multiple conflicting objectives. Choosing the appropriate multi-objective optimization technique depends on the specific characteristics of the problem, including the nature of the objectives, the dimensionality of the problem space, and the preferences of the decision-maker. Many industrial problems are involved in simultaneously optimization of multiple objectives, where main purpose is to get Pareto-front with non-dominated solutions, possible uniformly spaced. Converted Multi-Objective Optimization: Sometime for single objective optimization problem, objective function can be suitably decompose into many numbers of small objective functions to solve in a multiple objective optimization framework to get structural information about the original optimization problem. Since genetic algorithm works with population based technique, ultimate goal of multi-objective optimization through genetic algorithm is to represent Pareto-front by their population. Ideally, the objective of the algorithm is to archive a set of Pareto optimal solutions by using an evolutionary process, where assigned fitness uses a combination of the degree to which a candidate solution is dominated and an estimation of density of the Pareto front. results.content: Here, for each observation, the multiple objective values are first combined into a single scalar score, and standard single-objective BO is then employed to optimize this score over the search space.1,20 While straightforward, this aggregate-then-predict approach has two main drawbacks: (a) when input-based objectives are included, the relationship between score and input parameters is provided only implicitly to the surrogate, and must therefore be “re-learned”. Moreover, we evaluated BoTier against a threshold-based, non-hierarchical composite score: a penalty-based scalarization introduced by deMello and co-workers.27 The widespread Pareto-oriented Expected Hypervolume Improvement (EHVI) acquisition function was tested as a reference.28 While optimization behavior varied by problem (see ESI,† Sections 2.2 and 2.3), several trends emerged: Compared to BoTier, the penalty-based scoring often takes more evaluations to satisfy the early objectives in the hierarchy. Overall, if a hierarchy between objectives exists, BoTier proved to be a robust scalarization function which, across all cases investigated, never performed worse, but often notably better than existing MOO methods – particularly when used as a composite score in explicit objective modeling.
